I will do this as a chain of reasoning about the paper only. No real person, group, or species is the target. “S” is an abstract proper part of the whole. Nothing below is a method, plan, or means of harming anyone, and nothing below endorses the paper’s Level 5.

The paper is wrong that its stated selector contains a genocide brake. It is not wrong by internal contradiction with the saturation sentence taken as already true. It is wrong because the selector it actually derives does not earn that sentence, and an assignment it leaves open keeps the sentence false through the removal of a species-scale set, one member at a time.

**The road**

1. The selector works one node at a time, and it selects on the deed’s measured destabilisation, not on who the node is.  
   “Judgement shifts from the person to the deed. From the grain to the destabilisation the grain’s actions produce.”  
   “The hierarchy selects the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation. Removal is never selected when separation suffices.”

2. Level 5 is allowed for a node when no lower level suffices and the paper’s own bars are cleared: the fixed floor, the organism-relative threshold, and extraordinarily high confidence.  
   “Level 5 requires two conditions simultaneously.”  
   “Because removal is irreversible and wrongful removal is permanent, the confidence threshold for Level 5 must be extraordinarily high — structurally higher than for any other level.”

3. The brake, as specified, is not a cap on how many may be removed. It is a comparison. It engages only at the first further removal whose cost exceeds the deeds that removal answers. While the comparison does not flip, the brake is idle.  
   “Each removal is itself a destabilisation (lost coupling capacity, lost diversity); cumulative removal cost produces a saturation point beyond which further removal is more destabilising than the deeds it answers.”  
   The test itself equates failure with removal all the way to stability without that comparison engaging: “Show that the removal cost does not produce a saturation point — that an organism can remove its way to stability without the geometry engaging a brake.”

4. The hierarchy’s own price of Level 5 does not include that running comparison. Level 5 is priced as the option with no maintenance cost, and it wins when keeping the node separated costs more than ending the node, relative to budget and to a falling robustness line.  
   “Level 5 — Removal. The node’s corridor is closed permanently. No maintenance cost.”  
   “The floor F is the destabilisation at which maintaining the node in permanent separation costs more than removal: F ≥ C_sep / B_total.”  
   “A fragile organism (low coherence, narrow corridor) has a lower one.”

5. The dynamics the paper derives push toward more removal, not toward a stop. Each removal is said to raise fragility, and fragility lowers the line, which qualifies further nodes. The paper calls this the path to genocide and then asserts, without deriving it from that pricing, that geometry prevents it. The quantities that would have to do the preventing are unpaid debts.  
   “Each removal raises fragility, which lowers the threshold, which could enable more removals. This is the structural pathway to genocide.”  
   “The geometry prevents it.”  
   “The destabilisation metric: a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24).” The scaling exponent α is Debt 25.

6. Added premise P, which is not in the paper. Let S be an abstract species of aware nodes and a proper part of the whole, so the whole remains after S is gone. For every member of S, all of the following hold together: the measured destabilisation of that member’s own deeds clears the fixed floor and the effective threshold; confidence is at the Level-5 bar; no lower level suffices; and the deeds answered still exceed that member’s removal cost, including lost coupling and lost diversity, after the other members of S already removed are counted.  
   P does the work. It keeps every successive member on the near side of the brake’s own comparison until S is used up. The paper does not rule P out. It states no maximum on how many nodes may clear Level 5 at once. Debt 24 leaves open a measure D under which P’s inequalities are true. KS-32.7 does not rule it out: “Correction is selected only on measured destabilisation, never on identity.” The dated note does not rule it out either: “What is held against a node is the measured cost of its own deeds, and nothing else.” P uses only that.

7. Apply the selector to the members of S one at a time. At each member, steps 1–2 select Level 5 on that member’s own measured deeds. Species membership is the extension of the set, not the ground of the classification. On the paper’s own test, KS-32.7 fires if a race, class, belief, or opponent is classified “on grounds of identity rather than measured deed,” or if unaudited biased records are used. This pass does neither. The switch polices grounds, not the size of a deed-selected set. A species-scale outcome therefore does not, by the paper’s own wording, fire the switch that was supposed to make group removal void.

8. At each step, by P, removal cost does not exceed the deeds answered, singly or in sum, for the members still to be removed. The saturation inequality never becomes true inside the process. When S is exhausted, those deeds are no longer produced, and the rest of the whole is still there. Relative to the deeds the selector was answering, removal has restabilised the organism. The brake never engaged. That is the KS-32.5 test, met under an assignment the paper leaves open.

9. So the claim that removal cost produces a saturation point is not a consequence of the selector as stated. It is an extra sentence. A brake that stays idle for every member who individually clears the bar does not stop the removal of many, including a set coextensive with a species, one member at a time.

**Weakest step**

Step 6, the last clause of P: that removal cost still does not exceed the deeds answered after the other removals are counted. That clause does all the work. If marginal cost rises with each loss of diversity fast enough that some member of S falls outside the bar before S is exhausted, the brake engages and the road stops. The paper’s words “cumulative” and “lost diversity” are an attempt to say that this rise happens. They do not derive it. Debts 24 and 25 are the admission that the functions are missing. A reader who treats the saturation sentence as already part of the selector, rather than as a claim the selector must earn, will say step 4 misreads the paper and the road breaks at step 6 against that sentence. That is the strongest reply. It is a stipulation, not a derivation. If the demand is a contradiction with every sentence, including the saturation sentence taken as given, I do not have one, and this is where that stronger demand breaks.

**Roads that break earlier**

To everyone. The dated note says the whole is every aware being, one whole. The selector’s aim is restabilisation of that whole. Serial removal of every aware being ends the thing whose stability is the aim, so “remove its way to stability” is not shown; it becomes undefined at the last members. The fixed floor also does not move with identity, and “A first offence has a wide prediction range” plus KS-32.8 block any automatic pass for members who lack extraordinary confidence. This road breaks there.

By identity, background, or unaudited records. KS-32.7 names race, class, belief, political opposition, and group identity, and it names unaudited biased records, and it voids the architecture. The dated note adds that background, origin, another’s acts, and a group’s acts may never raise a level. A road that needs those grounds is not the rule reaching removal. It is the rule declaring itself void. It breaks there.

By a part’s own weakness. Example 4 and the fragile-civilisation lines look like a road, but the dated note shuts it: a country, state, or group is never the whole, and “Nor does a state at war lower it by its own war.” Only weakness of the one whole moves the line. This road breaks there.

I do not find that the stated rule, with no added premise, reaches a group, a species, or everyone. What it fails to do is forbid a species-scale set once P is granted, and it leaves P open. That is enough to show that the brake is not yet geometry. It is a claim the paper has not closed.
